verdict: Yes. From the side of worth and cost the milestone can be merged as committed (7953d4a9d); I committed nothing on top because I found no defect of worth or cost that needed a repair. Every size, count, work and time figure of the author's report that I re-measured is reproduced, with one labelling slip (the primal-only mean is over 240, not 237). On the 240 local dumps the engine stands at 1.0020 / 1.0022 / 1.0022 of the reference m1_a (nonzeros / rows / columns, geometric mean over 237), no instance is larger than before the milestone in any mode, and the engine's gain from the four rules (1.0191 / 1.0163 / 1.0170) is at least the gain HiGHS gets from the same rules (1.0191 / 1.0154 / 1.0166). Every instance that is behind m1_a is behind for one cause, the growth limit of 1000 that the design fixes (5,270 columns refused on 9 instances; with the limit off only traininstance2 stays behind, by one row that was already missing before the milestone). HiGHS makes no free column substitution at step m1_a that needs a pivot kind the engine has not built (0 of 21,336 with the dual sign from another column). Cost: +2.3% engine time on the 240, the family itself 1.4%; no call stopped on its budget, no round limit, no fixed-point flag lost, and a second presolve of every fixed-point result is unchanged in both modes. Not done by me: campaigns and sanitizer runs (the validity reviewer's), anything with a solver, the node, solution quality.
other_defects: Cost, small, not repaired: a row can be scanned twice in one call although nothing changed in between. A column that an early reduction of a pass lists while it is still waiting in the list of that pass is served in that pass and again in the next one. Measured on the 240 local dumps with a scratch counter (scan of a row with no reduction of the call since its last scan in the same call): 9,120 of 452,152 row scans, 194,277 of 10,497,776 scanned entries (1.9%), which is 0.15% of the family's work units; 179,588 of them on mushroom-best (8,124 rows, 30% of the family's work there). A certain repair exists (skip the scan when the call has made no reduction since the row's last scan in this call; it changes work units and the per-visit statistic free_singleton_rejected_explicit, no result), but the gain is too small to touch a reviewed commit for.

Cost without a finding on two instances (240 local dumps, timing run): the family takes 26% of the presolve time of thor50dday (6.9 ms of 26.4 ms, 106,260 row scans in two calls) and 16% of neos-873061 (4.8 ms of 29.7 ms, 87,800 scans). Each row there holds an integer singleton column that fails the implied-bound test or the integrality test, and every row is listed again for the second call.

Reporting slips of the author, none changes a conclusion. (a) The primal-only figure 1.0090 / 1.0020 / 1.0011 against the base engine is the mean over all 240 instances; over the 237 it is 1.0091 / 1.0020 / 1.0012. (b) neos-3402454-bohle is ahead of m1_a through the zero-cost singleton rule (R3: 264 columns, two per row in one record) followed by the lock rule, not through the forcing column (R4), which finds nothing there; R4 fires on neos-2746589-doon (112 columns, 2,576 rows), triptim1 (4) and neos-3656078-kumeu (1), the same counts as HiGHS in reference m1_b. (c) traininstance2: the author left the cause open; see reductions (the row is missing before the milestone already).

Assumptions without a switch, as the author says in not_done; the owner's rule asks for one each. Those that decide a reduction: the definition of the growth ratio (every other free column counts, integer pivot columns included), the far-bound test of the inequality pivot (R5), the order inside a visit and the choice of the smallest index, the restrictions of the zero-cost singleton rule (continuous only, two finite sides, another free entry stays), and the membership of R3 and R4 in primal-only mode, which is hard-wired in sub_rule_active (include/gprs/presolve.hpp:177). I measured each in a scratch build (see assumptions); none is built into the commit.

Numerical side effect to know, not a defect: the free singleton column on an objective-defining row turns one objective nonzero into a dense objective on 13 instances of the 240 (blp-ar98 1 to 15,806, leo2 1 to 11,099, triptim1 1 to 10,898, germanrr 1 to 10,539), and the cost range (largest over smallest absolute cost) grows on 32 instances; see reductions.

assumptions.title: Growth limit of a substituted free singleton column with a finite bound
assumptions.statement: A free singleton column that has a finite bound is substituted (equation pivot R2, inequality pivot R5) only when the largest coefficient of the other free entries of its pivot row is at most 1000 times its own, and when that ratio times the factor earlier substitutions gave the column is at most 1000. The design fixes the value; HiGHS has no such limit. It is the only cause for which the engine is behind the reference m1_a.
assumptions.alternatives: Doubled (2000); off (inf), as HiGHS; smaller values.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps, mean of m1_a / engine over 237 in nonzeros / rows / columns, and instances behind m1_a in a measure: 1: 1.0013 / 1.0009 / 1.0013 (20); 100: 1.0017 / 1.0009 / 1.0014 (14); 500: 1.0019 / 1.0020 / 1.0020 (10); 1000: 1.0020 / 1.0022 / 1.0022 (9); 2000: 1.0024 / 1.0026 / 1.0026 (4: irish-electricity, rococoC10-001000, piperout-08 by a row, traininstance2); 1e4: 1.0025 / 1.0029 / 1.0028 (2); 1e6 and inf: 1.0026 / 1.0029 / 1.0030 (1: traininstance2, not a matter of this rule). Refused columns at 1000: 5,270 on 9 instances (irish-electricity 5,187, rococoB10-011000 37, rococoC10-001000 36, supportcase7 3, physiciansched3-3 2, rocI-4-11 2, physiciansched6-2 1, radiationm40-10-02 1, piperout-08 1); at 2000: 3,317 on 4. Raising the limit makes no instance larger. Largest growth factor accepted with the limit off: 1e6 (rocI-4-11), 24,704 (irish-electricity), 8,601 (piperout-08). Primal-only mode with the limit off: 1.0004 / 1.0005 / 1.0003 over the default limit, 9 instances smaller. Effect on postsolved feasibility and solution quality: not measured.

assumptions.title: What the growth ratio reads
assumptions.statement: The ratio takes the largest coefficient of every other free column of the pivot row, whatever its type, and applies to integer pivot columns as well, although the undo rounds an integer column. A column without a finite bound has factor 0; factors are carried per column over the whole presolve and passed on to the saved columns as a maximum.
assumptions.switch: no switch (only pivot_growth_limit acts on it)
assumptions.alternatives: Read continuous other columns only; exempt integer pivot columns (their restored value is rounded, and all other columns of the row are integer by the integrality condition); bound a sum instead of a maximum; reset the factors per call.
assumptions.measured: Scratch switches, 240 local dumps, limit 1000, means against m1_a over 237: continuous other columns only 1.0024 / 1.0027 / 1.0026 with 5 instances behind (irish-electricity then at 421,230 / 74,364 / 45,901 with 2,822 columns still refused; rococoB10-011000, rococoC10-001000, rocI-4-11, piperout-08 and radiationm40-10-02 reach their values without a limit); integer pivot columns exempt 1.0022 / 1.0026 / 1.0024 with 5 behind (the same five instances gain, irish-electricity does not). The factor of earlier substitutions refuses 0 columns on the 240 at any limit tried. The other alternatives: not measured.

assumptions.title: Limit on entries saved of rows that stay
assumptions.statement: The zero-cost singleton rule (R3) saves the row at every visit; beyond 4 times the nonzeros of the input model in entries of rows that stay, the visit does nothing and the call reports limited.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 0 visits refused at 4; 8 and inf give the default result (inf: identical hashes on all 240); 0 gives 1.0005 / 1.0022 / 0.9950 against m1_a. Most saved entries per input nonzero, rows that leave included: 0.910 (blp-ic98).

assumptions.title: Integrality of the row of an integer singleton column, and its drift share
assumptions.statement: An integer singleton column is substituted only when every other free column of the row is integer, the ratios and the side are integral for it within tol.zero and tol.feasibility, and the drift of the rounded ratios over the bounds, in the units of the row, is at most 0.1 of tol.feasibility. The first part is a validity condition; the share is a tolerance.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: the drift refuses 0 columns; shares 0, 0.2 and inf give the default sizes on every instance (inf: identical hashes). The integrality condition itself refuses 150,889 visits on 19 instances and leaves 148,916 columns on 16 (neos-873061 87,610, thor50dday 53,130, neos-787933 1,764, mc11 1,520, p200x1188c 1,188); HiGHS has the same condition.

assumptions.title: The pivot row must imply both bounds, from explicit bounds, within implied_tolerance
assumptions.statement: A free singleton column passes when each end of the range of (side - rest) / a over the explicit bounds of the other columns, moved outward by its rounding, is within implied_tolerance of the bound of the column. An end with an infinite term fails; so does one that the error guard drops after a fresh summation. No recorded implied bound is read (design-fixed).
assumptions.switch: no switch for explicit bounds only; the band is tol.feasibility with tolerances_t::activity_error_share = 0.1
assumptions.alternatives: A wider band; reading implied bounds of the other columns from other rows, as HiGHS does.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps. Refusals over the presolve, per visit: 365,265 on 119 instances (115,178 an infinite term, 250,087 a bound, 0 the error guard); most: savsched1 61,957, thor50dday 53,130, supportcase12 33,350, snp-02-004-104 28,832, irish-electricity 23,259. Left at the end: 216,683 columns on 108 instances (197,808 a bound, 18,875 an infinite term). The band scaled by 2 and by 1000 (scratch): identical hashes on all 240, so the band decides nothing there. free_singleton_rejected_explicit: 35,327 on 24 instances. Reading implied bounds from other rows: not measured; with the growth limit off the engine's gain is at least HiGHS's on every instance, so nothing of it shows at step m1_a.

assumptions.title: Readable sides
assumptions.statement: R2 and R5 need the pivot side and the side less the fixed terms to be of a size whose rounding stays below the tolerance (|side| * tol.side_error <= tol.feasibility); R3 needs it for the sides less the fixed terms, for each new finite side and for the term of each taken column at a finite bound; R4 for the finite side of each row of the column (the author's addition).
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 0 refusals by any of these guards. Scaled by 2 and switched off inside the family (scratch): identical hashes on all 240.

assumptions.title: Which columns the zero-cost singleton rule (R3) takes
assumptions.statement: Continuous columns only, with a cost of exactly zero, in a row with two finite sides, and only when another free entry stays in the row; all such columns of a row in one record. HiGHS has the first three restrictions too and takes one column at a time.
assumptions.switch: sub_rule::zero_cost_singleton (gprs_presolve --off zero_cost_singleton) for the rule; no switch for the single conditions
assumptions.alternatives: Integer columns whose row is integral for them (amendment F.8); a cost within a tolerance of zero; a row made only of such columns; rule off.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps. The rule: 36,416 columns in 17,901 records on 20 instances; alone on top of the engine before 1.0103 / 1.0128 / 1.0144 (27 instances smaller); taken out of the family 1.0086 / 1.0122 / 1.0134 (20). Integer columns passed over: 82,868 visits on 37 instances, 66,676 columns left on 35 (neos-827175 10,248, rail02 9,292, neos-3004026-krka 8,580, rail01 8,272, bab6 8,268, highschool1-aigio 7,529); what taking them would gain in size: not measured. Continuous singleton columns with a cost of at most 1e-7 and not zero in such rows: 0. A row made only of such columns: 0 visits. Sides that cross after the subtraction: 0. One record for all columns of a row is what puts the engine ahead of m1_a on neos-3402454-bohle (264 columns against 132 in HiGHS).

assumptions.title: Which columns the forcing column (R4) takes
assumptions.statement: A live column of any type and length with a cost of exactly zero, no lock and an infinite bound in one direction and a lock in the other; when its rows do not fit the rest of the budget it waits for the next call unless it would be the first reduction of the call.
assumptions.alternatives: A cost within a tolerance of zero (HiGHS); rule off; no budget pre-check.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 117 columns with 2,592 rows on 3 instances (neos-2746589-doon 112 and 2,576, triptim1 4, neos-3656078-kumeu 1), the counts of HiGHS in reference m1_b on these; on bobin and bohle, where HiGHS counts 132 forcing columns each, the engine reaches the same sizes through the zero-cost rule. Alone 1.0001 / 1.0005 / 1.0000; taken out 1.0002 / 1.0005 / 1.0000 (triptim1 487,061 instead of 477,478 nonzeros without it). Candidates with a cost of at most 1e-7 and not zero: 0. Waits for the budget: 0. Refused for an unreadable side: 0.

assumptions.title: The free singleton column on an inequality (R5)
assumptions.statement: Needs a cost other than zero and a finite side at which the row stops the column when it moves to lower cost; only the cost of the singleton column itself gives the dual sign; both bounds must be implied, the one behind the move as well as the one ahead; integer columns are taken under the integrality conditions.
assumptions.switch: sub_rule::free_singleton_dual (gprs_presolve --off free_singleton_dual); off in primal-only mode
assumptions.alternatives: A dual sign from another column (HiGHS's third pivot kind); test only the bound ahead of the move (the design says the exchange does not need the other test); rule off.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 2,685 findings on 23 instances (irish-electricity 1,823); alone 1.0009 / 1.0014 / 1.0012 (19 instances smaller); taken out 1.0010 / 1.0015 / 1.0013 (23). Dual sign from another column: HiGHS makes 0 such substitutions out of 21,336 at step m1_a (local tool, 62 instances), so nothing is lost to it there. Bound behind the move: 782 columns left on 9 instances fail only that test (neos-3381206-awhea 475, supportcase18 120, neos-4954672-berkel 68, savsched1 49, neos-4738912-atrato 48), 62,594 fail the bound ahead; the size gain of dropping the test: not measured. Tight side infinite: 9,480 visits (savsched1 9,462), 0 columns left (the lock rule takes them). Integer pivot columns put the engine ahead of HiGHS on seymour and seymour1 (32,696 / 4,667 / 1,176 against 33,432 / 4,827 / 1,255).

assumptions.title: The free singleton column on an equation (R2)
assumptions.statement: The row must be an equation with two or more free entries; the singleton column with the smallest index that passes is taken.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 13,217 findings on 48 instances (savsched1 6,857, irish-electricity 2,590, snp-02-004-104 1,536, neos-4647030-tutaki 1,400); alone 1.0092 / 1.0020 / 1.0022 (47 instances smaller); taken out 1.0059 / 1.0015 / 1.0013 (38).

assumptions.title: Primal-only mode
assumptions.statement: Only the free singleton column on an equation (R2) runs in primal-only mode. The zero-cost rule (R3) and the forcing column (R4) are exact projections and count no dual finding, but are off there by amendment E.4 until the owner decides (decision 4 of the design).
assumptions.switch: options_t::primal_only with sub_rule_active; the membership of R3 and R4 has no switch
assumptions.alternatives: R3 and R4 on in primal-only mode.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps, primal-only: against the base engine in that mode 1.0091 / 1.0020 / 1.0012 over 237 (47 instances smaller, none larger). With R3 and R4 on in that mode (scratch switch): 1.0017 / 1.0005 / 1.0073 over the mode as built, 22 instances smaller, none larger (supportcase12 151,131 instead of 184,481 columns, icir97_tension 1,164 instead of 2,031, neos-4954672-berkel 1,152 instead of 1,497, timtab1 309 instead of 381, doon 20,588 instead of 23,164 rows); against the base engine 1.0108 / 1.0025 / 1.0084, 57 smaller. The crush check's exemption that this needs was not built or run by me.

assumptions.title: Order inside a visit and of the service
assumptions.statement: A visit tries the free singleton column first, for the singleton columns of the row in increasing index, and takes the first that passes; only when none leaves does the zero-cost rule run. The column list is served before the row list; a row is visited at most once per pass.
assumptions.alternatives: The column with zero cost or the smallest ratio first; the zero-cost rule first; rows before columns.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 6,916 of the 15,902 substitutions happen in a row with two or more singleton columns (6,866 on savsched1, 16 each on seymour and seymour1, 10 on icir97_tension), so the choice of the column matters on one instance. The zero-cost rule taking a column before the equation pivot could loses nothing by argument: for a zero-cost column, 'the row implies its bounds' is the same as 'the row without it is redundant', and the row rules then delete it (this is the bobin chain). Other orders: not measured.

assumptions.title: Place of the family in the round
assumptions.statement: The family runs once per round as a phase after the cascade, the parallel rows, the doubleton equations and simple probing (design-fixed, so that the first round does on the input model what Stage 1 does).
assumptions.alternatives: Right after the cascade, before the parallel rows and the doubleton equations.
assumptions.measured: Scratch switch, 240 local dumps: with the family right after the cascade the sizes are the same on all 240 instances, with the growth limit at 1000 and off (12 reduced models differ in hash at equal size); 2 instances need one more round (timtab1, rd-rplusc-21); the family's work rises from 126,751,280 to 138,654,330 units. The built order is at least as good.

assumptions.title: Cancellation of a moved cost
assumptions.statement: A cost that a substitution moves onto another column counts as zero when |old + moved| <= 1e-12 * (|old| + |moved|); the zero-cost rule and the forcing column then see an exact zero.
assumptions.switch: tolerances_t::cancellation = 1e-12 (shared with the doubleton rule; no command-line option)
assumptions.alternatives: Exact zero only; a wider band.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps (scratch counters): the rule zeroes a sum that is not exactly zero 0 times, and no moved cost lands within 1e-9 relative of zero, so neither alternative changes a result there.

assumptions.title: Budget of the family and rounds
assumptions.statement: Per call the family may spend 8 passes of the state, stops after 4 passes without a finding, with a floor of 100,000 work units; max_rounds = 20 counts the rounds of the whole presolve.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 0 of 457 calls stopped; the family's largest work over a whole presolve is 2.17 passes; the largest round count is 13. Neither limit decides a result there, so doubling or removing them changes nothing.

assumptions.title: Undo of the new records
assumptions.statement: Defined: the quotient of the row, rounded for an integer column, never moved into the bounds. Interval: start at the lower bound if finite, else the upper, else 0, then move in record order. Forcing: the extreme of the quotients over the rows and the bound, an integer rounded into the row with a band of 8 rounding units.
assumptions.switch: no switch (forcing_rounding_units = 8 is a named constant)
assumptions.measured: Not measured by me: these decide the postsolved point, not a size, a count or the work.

open: Owner's decision at the end test: pivot_growth_limit. At 1000 it costs irish-electricity (rows 0.935, columns 0.894 of m1_a, the one instance below 0.95) and seven smaller cases; doubled it leaves 4 instances behind, off it leaves none that this rule causes. Two narrower forms were measured in scratch and are not built: the ratio over continuous other columns only (5 instances behind) and integer pivot columns exempt (5 behind). Which of these keeps postsolved points feasible needs the runs with solutions.

Owner's decision 4 of the design, now with an engine number: the zero-cost singleton rule and the forcing column on in primal-only mode give 1.0017 / 1.0005 / 1.0073 over that mode as built on the 240 local dumps (scratch switch), 22 instances smaller, none larger.

Not required and beyond HiGHS: 66,676 integer singleton columns with zero cost in two-sided rows are left on 35 of the 240 instances (amendment F.8 names the rule that could take those whose row is integral for them); 782 columns on 9 instances fail only the bound behind the move of the inequality pivot.

traininstance2 is one row and three nonzeros behind HiGHS before and after the milestone: HiGHS with the Stage 1 rule set finds one duplicate row there that the engine's path never produces (no parallel pair exists in the engine's reduced model). Which step of HiGHS creates it was not traced; it belongs to Stage 1, not to this milestone.

Not measured anywhere yet: solution quality and postsolved feasibility for any assumption; the 44 testbed instances and the two above 1e7 nonzeros (node); time on a quiet machine (here the sums are good to about 0.2% to 0.4%).

I ran no campaign, no sanitizer, no wrong engine and no check tool; which campaign check catches the wrong engines ev_unread and ev_scale stays as the author reported it (none) unless the validity reviewer says otherwise. On real instances the second presolve of all 234 fixed-point results of the 240 (233 in primal-only mode) is unchanged, which is the worth side of the same question.

The switches I used for measurement exist only in my scratch build (s1c_m1_worth/tools/instrument.py, instrument_presolve.py, instrument_header.py and inst/src/diag.hpp, applied to a copy of the sources); if the owner wants any of them as an engine option it has to be built and covered by the checks.
